description:
Run a program of yours when something happens to you (a hook; only yours, your definition does not change). Changes work from the next event. The program is a tool folder or an executable; it gets the event as JSON on stdin (with "event", "hook", "stack" and the fields below). Events:
- before_queue: a message is about to enter your conversation (fields letter, content)
- after_queue: a message entered your conversation (letter, content)
- before_tool: one of your tools is about to run (name, id, arguments)
- after_tool: a tool finished, before you see its result (name, id, arguments, content, code, timed_out)
- brain_failed: your brain call failed (name = the error code, reason)
- tool_added: a tool name appeared in your tool box (name, path)
- after_start: your loop started; after_stop: your loop is about to exit (code, signal)
- on_clock: a clock moved on: give every_cycles or every_ms (counted in clock cycles); clock is optional (default: your daemon's clock); fields clock, cycle, interval_ms, first, last_cycle, missed. It runs once right after you start or wake up, then every N. It shows you nothing; to hear about it, let the program send a letter to your queue (aos-post send STACK/queue).
One op per call:
- list: {"op": "ls"}  (add "long": true to also see hooks you turned off)
- show one: {"op": "get", "name": "guard"}
- add: {"op": "add", "event": "before_tool", "path": "hooks/guard", "condition": "agents_ctl"}  (relative paths start at your workspace; condition = only for this tool name or error code)
- remove: {"op": "rm", "name": "guard"}
- back to your original hooks: {"op": "reset"}
The program's answer counts by default (before_queue, before_tool, after_tool; other events only tell it): exit 0 with empty stdout = no change, with a JSON object on stdout changes the event (content, or arguments for before_tool); exit 10 blocks it (the message is dropped / the tool does not run). "intercept": false = it is only told and its stdout is ignored. Any other exit code is a failure: by default you stop (on_error "continue" = only a warning).
Errors: ArgumentsBad, OpUnknown, PathMissing, HookExists (add "replace": true to replace it), HookMissing, HooksMissing, HooksBad, NameBad, DaemonMissing, DaemonFailed, InstanceMissing.

op.description: ls = list, get = show one, add = add one, rm = remove one, reset = undo all your changes

name.description: get, rm: the hook name. add: the name to call it by (default: the folder or file name; needed with path_json)

event.description: add: the event that runs it

path.description: add: the tool folder or executable to run; relative paths start at your workspace

path_json.description: add, instead of path: a value kept as written, like {"$env": "AOS_HOME", "$path": "/lib/x"}

condition.description: add: run only for this tool name (before_tool, after_tool, tool_added) or error code (brain_failed), or an array of them; not for queue events

intercept.description: add: false = only tell it, ignore its answer (default true: on before_queue, before_tool, after_tool its answer can change or block the event)

async.description: add: true = start it and do not wait (its answer is then never read)

on_error.description: add: when the program fails: stop (default, you stop) or continue (a warning)

timeout_ms.description: add: give up waiting after this many ms (default 60000; 0 = no limit)

replace.description: add: true replaces a hook you already have with the same name

long.description: ls: true = one text line per hook with all its settings, including hooks you turned off (null)

every_cycles.description: add, on_clock only: run when the clock moved this many cycles since the last run

every_ms.description: add, on_clock only: the same in ms, counted in clock cycles (not the wall clock)

clock.description: add, on_clock only: a proc name on your daemon table whose stack has a clock file, or the path of a clock file or a folder with one (relative = from your stack); default your daemon's clock (AOS_CLOCK)
